A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe D3DR for diffusion-guided 3DGS object insertion. All 20 pages of v1 and 34 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic 3D insertion experiments, real-image cup editing, baseline comparisons, timing measurements and ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and real 3D insertion results, component ablations, shadow evaluations, diffusion-model comparisons and personalization experiments.

M1.justification: v1 uses one personalized diffusion model followed by 2-step-DDS. v2 introduces two LoRA-personalized models, an additional image-conditioning convolutional branch for texture preservation, SDEdit refinement, and optimizable scene-shadow parameters with pruning (Sections 3.2–3.5). These substantially change the architecture and optimization procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the ten synthetic scenes and tiny real-image cup dataset, but adds captured real 3D insertion scenes involving a toaster, fabric bin and chair (Section 4.1; Table 7). This extends evaluation from synthetic 3D environments to real reconstructions, beyond the existing 2D real-image demonstration.

E2.justification: The main comparison expands from TIP-Editor and R3DG in v1 to those methods plus Copy-Paste, Latent Bridge Matching and Instruct-GS2GS in v2. All three additions participate in the reported synthetic comparisons, not merely citations or evaluations on the new real dataset.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: class-preservation images decrease from 200 to 32, rough personalization increases from 500 to 1,000 iterations, and 3DGS optimization changes from 20,000 to 3,000 steps including refinement. v2 also modifies TIP-Editor settings, adds cropped PSNR and shadow/background metrics, and revises the stated DTIS definition to compare image and text feature differences. SSIMpart is retained under the name SSIMcropped.

E4.justification: v2 adds texture-preservation and shadow ablations, quantitative shadow analysis, cropping-strategy comparisons, failure cases and diffusion-backbone sensitivity experiments (Section 4.4; Appendices B–D, K–L). Backbone tests cover SD1.5–2.1 in 3D and extend through SD3.5 in 2D. Existing personalization, IC-Light and DDS analyses remain, while v1's explicit mean-initialization ablations are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Additional scene averages and result tables in v2 do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 reports revised synthetic PSNRpart averages: D3DR changes from 8.863 to 11.966, TIP-Editor from 8.205 to 6.960, and R3DG from 8.406 to 8.598. These accompany revised methods/settings and are not controlled cross-version gains. v2 adds real-scene, shadow and component results, and reports 40 rather than 50 minutes for D3DR in Table 2.

T1.justification: The original SDS/DDS formulation is retained apart from notation. Appendix H adds rectified-flow definitions and corresponding SDS/DDS expressions, while Section 3.5 formalizes the assumption that affected scene Gaussians can only darken. These provide a limited extension of the mathematical setup; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 elevates inherent zero-shot harmonization and a novel texture-preserving personalization technique to explicit contributions, alongside the retained insertion method and dataset. Its conclusion extends validation claims to real scenes. The abstract replaces the claimed 0.5 PSNR/0.15 SSIM advantage with a 2.0 dB PSNR advantage against the revised comparison set.

C2.justification: v2 expands v1's scattered color and texture failure observations into explanations of IC-Light-induced albedo changes, texture oversmoothing, ambiguous illumination and unsupported dynamic scenes (Appendix D). It adds a camera-pose-noise hypothesis for missing real-scene shadows and discusses the tradeoff between shadow realism and background similarity (Appendices B–C, J).

D1.justification: v2 supplies LoRA, refinement, cropping and shadow settings, real-capture instructions, new baseline adaptations, original SceneNet identifiers, and code/project hyperlinks. However, v1's explicit initial DN-Splatter training and regularization settings and per-scene prompt list are omitted. Reproducibility information is substantially revised, with both additions and losses.

R1.justification: v2 positions the work as discovering another hidden zero-shot capability of diffusion models. It adds substantive discussions of LBM, Instruct-GS2GS and complementary language-guided placement through PlaceIt3D, plus references supporting texture personalization and rectified-flow adaptation. This substantially broadens v1's positioning around DDS, TIP-Editor and R3DG.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, method explanations and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The cup experiments are integrated into the method explanation, baseline configurations move to an appendix, and the appendices are reorganized around evaluation, limitations and implementation. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column journal layout, redraws the pipeline, restructures the main results into dataset averages with separate appendix tables, and consolidates qualitative comparison grids. It adds displays for personalization, model variants, failures, cropping and optimization schedules. Existing cup and SDS illustrations are also rearranged.

improvement.justification: v1's 3D evaluation was synthetic-only, used two comparators and showed unresolved texture failures. v2 addresses texture preservation with a dedicated component and ablations, adds real-capture evaluation and a copy-paste control alongside additional competitors, and documents failure mechanisms. These substantially strengthen validation and explanation. Mixed shadow/background scores (Tables 3–4), omitted reproduction details and changed experimental settings limit some conclusions, but do not outweigh those gains.
